prompts: Use case: identity-preserve. Production 16-bit fighting game sprite sheet, transparent background. Reference 1 is the EXISTING Kike Parker sprite atlas: preserve EXACT character design, navy suit, white shirt, red tie, lapel pin, short receding black hair, same face and anatomy, same pixel density and pixel-art rendering. Reference 2 is a real small tigrillo/ocelot for the spotted tan/black fur, large ears, long tail. Create a new sprite sheet strictly organized in 6 columns x 4 rows, 24 separate equal cells, no labels, no text, no borders. Every sprite entirely within its cell, generous clear gap between sprites, all facing RIGHT. Row 1 six distinct continuous WALK FORWARD cycle frames, natural legs and arms, hands in fighting guard; row 2 six distinct WALK BACKWARD cycle frames (still facing RIGHT, cautious backwards steps). Row3: columns1-4 four airborne FLYING KICK animation frames, launch knee, extend FRONT leg horizontally, fully straight extended flying sidekick, recoil; columns5-6 two downward open-hand SUMMON gesture frames. Row4: columns1-6 six fluid SUMMON animation frames: stern talking face, raises right hand, raises both hands, spreads hands as magical golden sparks emerge, points forward ordering tigrillos, returns toward guard. Full bodies no cropping, identical character head size across cells, no tigrillos on this particular sheet. Crisp nearest-neighbor pixel art, original 16-bit arcade aesthetic, dark outlines, NO antialias or blur, no changes to costume or identity.

Use case: style-transfer. Asset type: transparent pixel art sprite sheet for a 16-bit arcade fighter. Reference photo: small tigrillo/ocelot, NOT an orange tiger: large round ears, golden tan fur with black rosette spots, white belly/muzzle, long ringed tail. Create exactly 16 sprites, arranged 4 columns by 4 rows on a transparent background with generous empty gaps between equal cells. All sprites face RIGHT, side view, whole body tail and paws entirely in cell, no text or labels. Rows 1 and 2 are eight DISTINCT sequential RUN CYCLE frames for the same small ocelot, stretch, gather, forepaw reach, hindleg drive etc. Row3 four sequential LEAP AND BITE frames, spring upwards, extend forepaws, open tiny mouth to bite in midair, recoil. Row4 four sequential CLAW ATTACK frames, reach right forepaw, slash forward, alternate other forepaw, land crouch. Animal looks fierce yet charming, plausible ocelot anatomy, natural four legs, consistent proportions/head size, crisp visible square pixels, dark outline, three-tone shading per color, tan/cream/dark brown palette, no blurry painted rendering, no speed FX integrated into body. It must match the pixel-art visual fidelity of the supplied Kike sprite atlas, which is reference 2.

Use case: identity-preserve. New combat sprite sheet for existing 16-bit fighting game, transparent background. Reference1 = Estrella in gray suit, red tie, white shirt, lapel pin, curly short black hair, clean-shaven smiling face; reference2 = Cardenas existing atlas, stocky/bearded glasses man in burgundy short sleeved polo, exposed small belly, blue jeans, black shoes and wristwatch. Preserve both original designs EXACTLY, same square pixel detail, same face/body colors/clothing. Strict grid 4 columns x 3 rows, 12 clearly separated equal cells. Row1 four sequential AIRBORNE FLYING SIDE KICK frames of ESTRELLA facing RIGHT: launch bent knee, partially extends FRONT leg, FULL straight leg horizontal to RIGHT with other leg tucked, recover bent leg. Row2 same four frames of CARDENAS facing RIGHT, heavy stocky body, glasses/beard, same burgundy polo and jeans. Row3 four sequential overhead descending strike frames of CARDENAS: winds up holding his tan canvas shoulder bag above/behind shoulder, lifts bag above head, swings bag diagonally down to RIGHT, finishes swing down and forward. Full body in all cells, keep head size consistent across row, avoid cropping/overlap/stray pieces entirely, generous empty spacing around each. No labels, no lettering, no backgrounds. Pixel art on transparent alpha. Crisp original 16-bit game style, no smoothing, no painterly render.

Use case: background-extraction. Edit target: the attached Kike Parker sprite sheet. Remove ONLY the white background and make it genuinely transparent (alpha=0), including all white/near-white empty gaps between all 24 sprites and within bent arms/legs. Preserve the sprites EXACTLY: same 6x4 cell layout and dimensions, same poses, pixel colors, face, navy suit, shirt, red tie, proportions, everything. White shirts and highlights INSIDE the characters must remain opaque. No redesign, no new pixels around characters, no shadows, no checkerboard painted in. This is purely a transparent cutout/export of the existing sheet.

Precise background replacement of this sprite sheet. Keep ALL 24 Kike sprites IDENTICAL, preserving all poses, placement, colors, face and clothing. Replace EVERY background pixel outside the character silhouettes with one FLAT SOLID PURE MAGENTA color RGB(255,0,255), hex #ff00ff. It is a technical chroma key sprite sheet: no transparent background, no gray, no white, no black background, NO gradients, NO shadows, NO glow, NO textures, NO vignette. Empty holes between arms and legs must also be pure magenta. Do not modify the white shirts INSIDE the sprite silhouettes. Layout remains 6 columns and 4 rows, exactly same canvas and placement. Remove diffuse glows behind magic sparkles, keep individual gold sparkle pixels. SOLID #FF00FF everywhere outside sprites. All actual character pixels must be preserved.
notes: Las variantes de fondo blanco y extracción con gradiente se descartaron; se utiliza la lámina con fondo magenta para extraer las celdas. Recorte técnico por celdas y alfa mediante canvas; no se rediseñan los sprites durante el recorte.
